```{r}
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project) != project) {
  project <- dirname(project)
}
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")))
restaurants <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/restaurant_ratings.csv"))
audit <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/audit_times.csv"))
restaurants$quality_rating <- factor(restaurants$quality_rating,
  levels = c("Good", "Very Good", "Excellent"), ordered = TRUE)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
```

## 1. Variable classifications

| Variable | Type | Discrete / continuous | Measurement level | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Restaurant identifier | Categorical | Not applicable | Nominal | Numbers identify units |
| Payment method | Categorical | Not applicable | Nominal | Labels have no inherent order |
| Quality rating | Categorical | Not applicable | Ordinal | Categories are ordered; gaps are not defined |
| Number of orders | Numerical | Discrete | Ratio | Integer counts; zero means no orders |
| Waiting duration | Numerical | Continuous underlying quantity | Ratio | Zero means no elapsed waiting; ratios of positive durations are meaningful |
| Celsius temperature | Numerical | Continuous | Interval | Equal differences; conventional zero |
| Calendar year | Numerical | Discrete as defined here | Interval | Integer years have meaningful differences, but no absolute zero |
| Delivery distance | Numerical | Continuous | Ratio | Zero distance and meaningful ratios |

The stored waiting durations have one-minute increments. Accept an answer that explicitly classifies **recorded rounded values** as discrete while recognizing the underlying duration as continuous. Do not teach “decimals = continuous” or “integer storage = discrete.” Discrete/continuous and measurement level answer separate questions.

## 2. Corrections

1. Quality codes preserve order only. The coding does not define equal distances or a meaningful zero. Changing the codes changes numerical ratios without changing restaurant quality.
2. Recorded precision does not determine the underlying quantity. Elapsed duration is continuous, although the stored observations are rounded to whole days.
3. Celsius has a conventional zero. A 10-degree difference has meaning; the ratio 20/10 changes if the same temperatures are converted to Fahrenheit. It does not establish “twice as hot.”

## 3. Toolbox choices

| Question | Suitable table | Suitable chart | Useful measures |
|---|---|---|---|
| Most common quality | Frequency / percentage table | Ordered bar chart | Mode, proportions |
| Audit duration | Grouped frequency table | Histogram or dot plot | Mean, median, sample SD, quartiles, IQR, range |
| Prices by quality | Summary table within each quality group | Side-by-side boxplots | Group medians and IQRs; means and SDs when appropriate |
| Advertising and sales | Paired observations | Scatterplot | Correlation as a descriptive measure of linear association |

Several defensible choices are possible. Assess whether the choice answers the question and respects the variable definitions. Reserve time-series line charts for questions about change over time.

## 4. Restaurant quality

```{r}
quality <- as.data.frame(table(restaurants$quality_rating))
names(quality) <- c("Quality", "Count")
quality$Percent <- 100 * quality$Count / sum(quality$Count)
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(quality$Count), c(84L, 150L, 66L)),
          sum(quality$Count) == 300, sum(quality$Percent) == 100)
kable(quality)
ggplot(restaurants, aes(quality_rating)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#2878A5", width = .65) +
  labs(title = "Restaurant quality ratings", x = "Quality rating", y = "Restaurants")
```

**Very Good** is the modal category: **150 restaurants (50%)**. A bar chart presents separate categories. A histogram treats its axis as numerical intervals and would suggest quantitative spacing between the codes.

## 5. Audit durations

```{r}
names(audit)
x <- audit$audit_days
stopifnot(length(x) == 20, !anyNA(x))
groups <- cut(x, breaks = seq(10, 35, 5), right = FALSE)
frequency <- as.data.frame(table(groups))
names(frequency) <- c("Days", "Frequency")
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(frequency$Frequency), c(4L, 8L, 5L, 2L, 1L)))
kable(frequency)
ggplot(data.frame(days = x), aes(days)) +
  geom_histogram(breaks = seq(10, 35, 5), closed = "left",
                 fill = "#2878A5", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Duration of 20 audits", x = "Audit duration (days)", y = "Audits")
q <- quantile(x, c(.25, .75), type = 6)
summary_values <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Mean", "Median", "Sample standard deviation", "Minimum", "Maximum",
              "Range", "Q1", "Q3", "IQR"),
  Days = c(mean(x), median(x), sd(x), min(x), max(x), diff(range(x)),
           q[1], q[2], diff(q)))
kable(summary_values, digits = 2)
stopifnot(mean(x) == 19.25, median(x) == 18, q[1] == 15, q[2] == 22)
```

The 20 audits took **19.25 days on average**, with a **sample standard deviation of `r round(sd(x), 2)` days**. Standard deviation describes spread around the mean; it is not a guarantee that every audit lies within one standard deviation. The middle half is described by Q1 = **15 days** and Q3 = **22 days**, an IQR of **7 days**.

The mean (19.25) exceeds the median (18). The longer observed durations, including 28 and 33 days, pull the mean upward. The histogram supports a longer right tail in these observations; mean versus median alone is not a universal test of shape.

## Teaching notes and source conventions

- Keep the first discussion about the **meaning of the variable**, before introducing R storage classes.
- Use the book's Section 1.2 for measurement levels and Section 5.1 for discrete/continuous quantities; introduce the latter early without probability calculations.
- The book uses the interior percentile position `(n + 1) * p`, matching R's `type = 6` interpolation for these quartiles. R's default uses a different convention. Explain small differences rather than treating all software output as identical.
- ggplot2 boxplots use their own default quartile convention. If comparing them to a `type = 6` table, explain the convention or construct boxplot statistics explicitly.
- The restaurant counts and audit observations are checked against the printed textbook examples. See the lesson's source note for the scope of the checks.
